The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum is a federally chartered, nonpartisan institution that was created by the US Congress to serve as America's national memorial to the victims of the Holocaust and an educational institution dedicated to the history and lessons of the Holocaust.

The Museum seeks to educate Americans from all 50 states and all walks of life as well as international audiences. The Museum has three areas of expertise: Holocaust remembrance, Holocaust scholarship and education, and genocide prevention.

In carrying out its important memorial and educational mission, the Museum is guided by its institutional values for our workplace: Honor the memory of the victims; carry out our work with dignity, humility, integrity and respect for others; and strive for excellence through teamwork, rigor, and a culture of continuous learning.

s.t:

s.t:
Assist in the month end reporting process to deliver timely and accurate information
Have full responsibility for a part of the revenue recognition process relevant to your strengths

Support the finance team's wider plans to prepare for an IPO
Improve the efficiency of financial processes and procedures and monitor compliance

Exceptional academic track record and subsequent career performance
Bachelor's degree in Accounting or equivalent
Qualified accountant (ACCA, ACA, ACMA, CPA, etc.)
IFRS 15/ASC 606 revenue recognition experience
Experience at a large public accounting firm, or public multinational corporate accounting department preferred
NetSuite or similar systems experience a plus
Willingness to travel up to four times per year

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR Basic Qualifications:You must meet the basic requirements listed below and also meet the minimum qualifications requirements. Basic Requirements A.

Degree: accounting; or a degree in a related field such as business administration, finance, or public administration that included or was supplemented by 24 semester hours in accounting. The 24 hours may include up to 6 hours of credit in business law. (The term "accounting" means "accounting and/or auditing" in this standard.

Similarly, "accountant" should be interpreted, generally, as "accountant and/or auditor.") -OR- B. Combination of education and experience: at least 4 years of experience in accounting, or an equivalent combination of accounting experience, college-level education, and training that provided professional accounting knowledge.

The applicant's background must also include one of the following: 1. Twenty-four semester hours in accounting or auditing courses of appropriate type and quality. This can include up to 6 hours of business law. 2. A certificate as Certified Public Accountant or a Certified Internal Auditor, obtained through written examination; or 3.

Completion of the requirements for a degree that included substantial course work in accounting or auditing, e.g., 15 semester hours, but that does not fully satisfy the 24-semester-hour requirement of paragraph A, provided that (a) the applicant has successfully worked at the full-performance level in accounting, auditing, or a related field, e.g., valuation engineering or financial institution examining; (b) a panel of at least two higher level professional accountants or auditors has determined that the applicant has demonstrated a good knowledge of accounting and of related and underlying fields that equals in breadth, depth, currency, and level of advancement that which is normally associated with successful completion of the 4-year course of study described in paragraph A; and (c) except for literal nonconformance to the requirement of 24 semester hours in accounting, the applicant's education, training, and experience fully meet the specified requirements.

Minimum Qualifications for GS-11: You must have one year of specialized experience to perform successfully the duties of the position.

To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the GS-09 grade level in the Federal service performing ALL of the following: Analyzing and reconciling financial data across multiple systems to ensure accuracy and completeness.

Investigating discrepancies and irregularities, determine root causes, and implement corrective actions.

Contributing to financial reporting, process improvements, and audit readiness with limited supervision. -OR- Education: Successful completion of at least three (3) years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. degree or Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree. -OR- Combination: Successful completion of a combination of graduate-level education (beyond the first two years) and specialized experience, as described above, to meet the total requirements.

The education portion must include graduate courses that demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do to the work of this position. Minimum Qualifications for GS-12: You must have one year of specialized experience to perform successfully the duties of the position.

To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the GS-11 grade level in the Federal service performing ALL of the following: Leading analysis and resolution of complex financial discrepancies and account issues.

Analyzing and reconciling complex financial data to ensure accuracy, consistency, and compliance with accounting principles and policies. Preparing and presenting financial reports, analyses, and trends to support leadership decision-making and communicate results to stakeholders.

Overseeing reconciliation processes and evaluating system outputs to ensure accuracy and reliability. Recommending and implementing process improvements that strengthen financial integrity and operational efficiency. Minimum Qualifications for GS-13: You must have one year of specialized experience to perform successfully the duties of the position.

To be creditable, specialized experience must have been equivalent to at least the GS-12 grade level in the Federal service performing ALL of the following: Performing advanced accounting assignments independently while managing competing priorities and deadlines.

Utilizing multiple accounting systems to post, track, validate, and reconcile financial transactions and records. Investigating and resolving complex discrepancies, unusual balances, and cross-system issues by identifying root causes and implementing corrective actions.

Providing technical guidance to staff and support audit readiness through documentation, internal controls, and accurate financial reporting. Leading process improvement initiatives and collaborating with stakeholders to enhance efficiency, strengthen controls, and improve overall financial operations.

Documenting experience: IN DESCRIBING YOUR EXPERIENCE, PLEASE BE CLEAR AND SPECIFIC. WE WILL NOT MAKE ASSUMPTIONS REGARDING YOUR EXPERIENCE. Qualifications are based on breadth/level of experience.

In addition to describing duties performed, applicants must provide the exact dates of each period of employment (from MM/YY to MM/YY) and the number of hours worked per week if part time.

As qualification determinations cannot be made when resumes do not include the required information, failure to provide this information may result in disqualification. Applicants are encouraged to use the USAJOBS Resume Builder to develop their federal resume.

Do not copy and paste the duties, specialized experience, or occupational application questionnaire from this announcement into your resume as that will not be considered a demonstration of your qualifications for this position.

In accordance with Office of Personnel Management policy, federal employees are assumed to have gained experience by performing duties and responsibilities appropriate for their official series and grade level as described in their position description.

Experience that would not normally be part of the employee's position is creditable, however, when documented by satisfactory evidence, such as a signed memorandum from the employee's supervisor or an SF-50 or SF-52 documenting an official detail or other official assignment.

The documentation must indicate whether the duties were performed full time or, if part time, the "percentage of times" the other duties were performed. It is expected that this documentation is included in the employee's official personnel record.

In order to receive credit for experience in your resume that is not within the official series and grade level of your official position, you must provide a copy of the appropriate documentation of such experience as indicated above.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through national Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; community; student; social).

Join the Finance Department as a Financial Accountant, reporting to the Accounting Team Lead, and help us maintain the highest standards of financial accuracy, compliance, and reporting excellence.
In this role, you will work in a fast-paced environment, managing a wide variety of accounting and financial reporting activities. You will use analytical skills in your day-to-day work, provide timely and accurate financial information to support decision-making, and proactively identify opportunities to improve processes and controls.
More broadly, your role will be to ensure that all business transactions and events relevant to the company's financial position are recorded accurately, comprehensively, and systematically. Together with your team, you will ensure compliance with applicable accounting principles, regulatory requirements, policies, and standards.
You will contribute to providing internal and external stakeholders with a clear and reliable view of the company's financial position and performance. As a Financial Accountant, you will also support senior management with financial planning, analysis, and reporting.

* Maintain general ledger, prepare journal entries and produce various accounting schedules/reconciliation in accordance with various GAAPSs either for the bank in Switzerland (IFRS and ARB-FINMA) or for one of the foreign subsidiaries (local GAAP).
* Prepare and review monthly, quarterly and annual financial closings. Actively participate in the half-year and year-end closing, with responsibility for specific topics and notes to the financial statements. This includes preparation of answers to external auditors.
* Investigate and resolve accounting discrepancies, unusual movements and ageing items.
* Review journal entries, accruals, provisions, prepayments and other accounting adjustments.
* Ensure appropriate accounting treatment for banking transactions and financial instruments.
* Support the preparation of statutory and management financial statements.
* Contribute to the preparation of consolidated financial reporting where applicable.
* Take responsibility in accounting projects as assigned by Management,
* Provide accounting guidance and implement appropriate solutions for complex accounting issues and queries raised by various departments and foreign group entities
* Prepare miscellaneous regulatory filings (for the SNB or FINMA as example) as assigned.

* Bachelor-s degree or equivalent diploma in accounting, finance or economics.
* Minimum 5 years- experience in a similar role ideally in the banking industry.
* You must be fluent in French and English (oral and written).
* You are adaptable and experienced in managing complex financial matters within a dynamic environment.
* You are meticulous, able to collaborate cross functionally and to work on several subjects in parallel, attentive to details with very good organisation skills.
* Strong understanding of the banking business, with the ability to see the bigger picture and understand the broader financial context.
* You have experience with IFRS and generally accepted accounting principles in Switzerland (Accounting Rules for Banks -ARB-FINMA- is a plus).
* Your skills in MS Office (Excel in particular) are excellent. Knowledge of PowerBI, SQL and/or Python are a plus.
* Knowledge of software Temenos T24 and OneStream is considered a plus.

Spreedly is the world's leading Open Payments Platform. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Durham, NC, the company gives mid-market and enterprise businesses the infrastructure to connect to any payment gateway, processor, or fraud tool through a single API. The platform is vendor-agnostic by design, meaning customers are never locked into a single provider and never need to rebuild their payments stack to access new capabilities.
The core business problem Spreedly solves is real and costly: global merchants face a fragmented payments ecosystem, where every new market, payment method, or fraud tool typically requires a separate, time-consuming integration. Spreedly eliminates that complexity, enabling companies to route transactions intelligently, secure cardholder data, prevent fraud, and expand into new markets without heavy engineering overhead.

Spreedly is the payment orchestration platform that lets merchants, platforms, and fintechs connect to hundreds of payment services through a single integration. As we modernize our finance systems, recently moving to Rippling and rolling out Ramp later this year, we are hiring a Senior Accountant to help run a lean, highly automated accounting function.
Reporting to the Accounting Manager, this is a broad, hands-on individual contributor role on a small team. Because routine general-ledger and accounts-payable work is increasingly automated, this role is less about manual data entry and more about ownership, judgment, exception handling, and continuous improvement of how we close the books. It is a strong fit for an accountant who is comfortable across the full close, curious about new systems, and eager to put automation and AI tools to work

Assist with the recurring month-end close: prepare and post journal entries, accruals, prepaids, and amortization; complete assigned account reconciliations; and investigate and explain variances.
Perform balance sheet and subledger reconciliations across the general ledger, ensuring items are supported, current, and cleared timely.
Support accounts payable, accounts receivable, and billing in an increasingly automated environment, including review, exception handling, and controls rather than manual invoice entry.
Process and administer company payroll, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance with applicable federal, state, and local regulations.
Record and reconcile payroll-related accounting entries (Rippling) and administer equity/stock (Carta), including related reconciliations and reporting.
Support day-to-day expense management, including reviewing, approving, and reconciling employee expense reports and corporate card transactions (e.g., in Ramp).
Take first pass on revenue recognition: enter and configure customer contracts in NetSuite under ASC 606, preparing schedules for the Controller's review and ownership.
Support the outsourced tax function by gathering schedules and requested documentation for our external provider.
Act as a power user across our finance systems (NetSuite, Rippling, Ramp), helping maintain configurations, troubleshoot, and keep integrations running cleanly.
Identify and implement process improvements: streamline close tasks, build automations, and pilot AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual effort and improve accuracy.
Support the annual audit and maintain clear process documentation for the areas you own.

4+ years of progressive accounting experience, including ownership of month-end close activities.
Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
Solid working knowledge of U.S. GAAP, including exposure to revenue recognition under ASC 606.
Hands-on experience with a major ERP; NetSuite strongly preferred.
Strong reconciliation and analytical skills, with high attention to detail and accuracy.
Comfort working in a lean, fast-changing environment where you own outcomes end-to-end.
Genuine curiosity about, and comfort experimenting with, AI tools and new systems, and eagerness to adopt them to work smarter. (You do not need to be an expert; we care about the mindset and aptitude.)

CPA (or active candidate)
Experience in SaaS, technology, or payments/fintech.
Experience using Anthropic's Claude in an accounting context.
Familiarity with our stack: Rippling, Ramp, Carta, Maxio, or comparable tools.
A track record of process improvement or automation — examples of manual work you eliminated or streamlined.

Additional Information

Spreedly provides an open payments platform. The platform’s connectivity provides payments performance. Key products and services include:
Connect — A unified API that integrates with hundreds of payment gateways, processors, and alternative payment methods worldwide, including digital wallets. Merchants access the global payments ecosystem through one connection.
Vault — A PCI-compliant secure repository for payment methods. Merchants store card data once and reuse it across any payment service, reducing PCI scope and protecting cardholder data at scale.
Optimize — Workflow-driven routing and retry logic that directs each transaction to the best-performing gateway in real time. On average, 7.9% of failed transactions succeed immediately when retried on a secondary gateway. This is where merchants recover lost revenue and increase authorization success rates.
Protect — A flexible fraud and authentication layer, incorporating advanced fraud tools and 3DS. Following Spreedly's acquisition of Dodgeball in September 2025, fraud orchestration and payment optimization now operate within the same platform.
Resolve — Centralized management and reporting that reduces operational silos, strengthens security, and improves billing control across a merchant's entire payment operation.

We describe our team as "Spreedlings": diverse, forward-thinking, and driven by a shared belief that a more open payments ecosystem benefits everyone. The company operates with a culture built on transparency, courageous collaboration, and self-driven leadership. The team values simplicity in both product and process, and approaches problem-solving with genuine curiosity.
--
We champion the ethical, creative use of AI—if you’re someone who pairs human judgment with modern AI tools to work smarter and drive bigger impact, you’ll thrive here.
--
Spreedly is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering, cultivating, and preserving a culture of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging. We actively work to drive out even unintentional discrimination in our hiring processes via practices like blindly graded work samples, structured interviews, and diversity awareness training.

About Radiant
Radiant is redefining how AI infrastructure is built. We design and operate AI-native infrastructure platforms engineered for sovereignty, performance, and scale — powering GPU-native workloads, multi-tenant control planes, and high-performance AI systems for the most demanding environments. We are building purpose-built AI infrastructure from powered land, to compute, to software.
As we scale our operations and deploy capital into the next generation of AI infrastructure, we are looking to expand our finance team with leaders who can combine technical strength with execution excellence and are driven to build.
Radiant was established by Brookfield, a leading global alternative asset manager with over US$1 trillion of assets under management across real estate, infrastructure, renewable power and transition, private equity and credit.

Brookfield's global relationships, investment expertise and access to long-term institutional capital provide Radiant with a differentiated platform from which to develop, finance and operate AI infrastructure assets.

This combination of entrepreneurial execution and institutional sponsorship enables Radiant to pursue large-scale GPU and AI infrastructure opportunities globally.

We're seeking a Senior Accountant to own core financial operations across Radiant's fast-scaling platform and help build the finance function as we grow. Working closely with the Head of Group Reporting, Finance Manager and senior finance management, you'll take full ownership of AR/AP, month-end and year-end close, reconciliations, and entity setup - ensuring accurate financial reporting, strong controls, and timely insights that enable business decisions.
This is a high-impact role for someone who wants to take real ownership, mentor junior team members, and shape how financial operations scale with rapid growth. You'll have visibility across the full finance function, work across multiple jurisdictions, and play a central role in audit processes and strategic reporting. If you are an experienced accountant who thrives on responsibility and wants to be a trusted leader in a fast-moving business, this is your opportunity.

Own Revenue & AR and Expenses & AP processes end-to-end, establishing robust controls, driving accuracy, resolving complex queries, and ensuring timely collections and payment approvals that maximize vendor relationships
Lead month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close processes, reviewing journals, accruals, and management schedules, and ensure all stakeholders have timely, accurate reporting
Oversee revenue billing and reconciliations, managing the complete cycle from billing accuracy to resolution external discrepancies
Take ownership of year-end financial statement preparation, including supporting schedules, disclosures, and technical accounting decisions
Act as the primary contact for external auditors, coordinating audit deliverables, resolving technical accounting questions, and driving resolution of audit matters
Lead the finance and accounting workstream for new global entity setups, navigating multi-jurisdictional complexity and establishing proper financial foundations from day one
Mentor and review work from junior team members, building their technical skills, quality control, and understanding of our accounting approach
Collaborate across the broader finance team and business stakeholders, building effective relationships and ensuring timely, accurate financial information flows across the organization
Drive continuous improvement in financial controls, accounting processes, and reporting procedures, identifying opportunities to enhance efficiency and strengthen our financial foundation.

Fully qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent) with 4-7 years of accounting experience, gained in public accounting or industry roles, ideally in multi-entity or international environments.
Strong Excel capabilities, accounting system knowledge, and ability to pick up new tools and processes quickly.
Strong technical accounting and financial reporting skills, you understand accounting standards and controls and can navigate complex transactions.
Meticulous attention to detail and accuracy, you maintain high standards while managing multiple priorities and deadlines.
Analytical thinking and problem-solving ability, you investigate issues thoroughly and drive resolution, often taking ownership of solutions.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management, you build trust with colleagues, external auditors, and senior management.
Natural mentor, you help junior team members develop skills, ask good questions, and take pride in building capability in others.
Strong organisation and time management, you juggle multiple work streams, manage competing deadlines, and ensure nothing falls through the cracks.

Experience with multi-entity consolidation and group financial reporting
Background with modern accounting platforms (Xero, NetSuite, or equivalent)
Exposure to energy, infrastructure, or capital-intensive industries
Experience with regulatory compliance across multiple jurisdictions
What Success Looks Like
Financial operations run smoothly, AR/AP is accurate and timely, month-end close happens predictably without fire-fighting, and senior management trusts the numbers.
Your junior team members are developing stronger skills and ownership, they come to you for guidance, and you're actively building their capability.
External auditors value you as a partner, they know you'll provide clean documentation, resolve queries promptly, and stand behind our accounting positions.
You've become the trusted voice on technical accounting matters, stakeholders across finance and operations come to you to understand complex transactions and financial implications.
You're shaping how the finance function scales, identifying process improvements, building stronger controls, and ensuring our accounting foundation supports rapid growth.

Competitive compensation including company-wide share scheme, bonus, travel paid
Work at the forefront of the AI infrastructure industry and take real ownership of a core function, building strategy and improvement across financial operations, not just executing processes.
Build and mentor a growing team, develop junior accountants and shape the culture and capability of the finance function

Develop your career in a Brookfield-backed company with resources, mentorship, and genuine growth opportunities

The Accountant: Conducts financial analyses, audits, and/or investigations of major foreign and/or domestic businesses; reviews, analyzes, and validates industry financial data. Designs, implements, and develops automated accounting systems. Provides expert advice in specialized areas of accounting, resolving problems, and developing policies.

Determines accounting system adequacy, reviews legislation and regulations and develops rules, procedures and guidelines for program users and develops and monitors internal accounting control program(s): identifying problem areas and developing solutions to improve operating program effectiveness.

Maintains complex operating accounting systems, which includes developing systems improvements, and providing solutions to program management problems and provides advice to financial and program managers and other accountants on unusual and difficult accounting systems and/or operations problems.

Develops procedural manuals, methods, and directives. Conducts independent studies for special projects and develops segments of surveys and systems for gathering and analyzing data; resolves accounting discrepancies in reported data.

The ideal candidate for this position possesses extensive experience in federal financial reporting and general ledger reconciliations, including SF-133s, DATA Act submissions, and year-end audit support.

Additionally, they bring demonstrated expertise in evaluating automated accounting systems, enhancing internal controls, and delivering strategic financial guidance to executive stakeholders.
To meet the minimum qualifications for this position, you must (1) meet the Education Requirement for the series, (2) provide a copy of transcripts for verification, AND/OR (3) meet the specialized experience requirements for the grade at which you are requesting consideration.

To qualify for the GS-11 on Experience, you must have at least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-09 it must include: Experience providing input for the monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements, including all supporting schedules; monthly SF-133s (Report on Budget Execution and Budgetary Resources); review of DATA Act submissions; and other Federal financial reports as needed.

Experience supporting the senior accountant with required financial reconciliations, report preparation and other financial documentation as needed.

Experience providing input for the annual financial statement audit, including assistance in responding to Prepared By Client (PBC) items, other audit requests for information, and assisting in providing information to the senior accountant to answer auditor inquiries.

To qualify for the GS-11 on Education alone, you must have: 3 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. degree or Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree. You can also qualify based on a combination of higher level graduate education and experience.

This must be fully supported by your resume and transcripts, provided with your application.

To qualify for the GS-12, you must have at least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-11, it must include: Experience reconciling financial accounts, including cash, accounts receivable, accounts payable, and resolving variances between subsidiary ledgers and general ledger control accounts.

Experience participating in the development, testing, or implementation of automated accounting system segments, policies, or data gathering procedures. Experience conducting financial analyses, audits, or investigations of domestic or foreign businesses by validating and evaluating industry financial data.

To qualify for the GS-13, you must have at least one year of experience equal or equivalent to the GS-12, it must include: Experience designing, implementing, or maintaining automated accounting systems, including reviewing legislation regulations, policies, or procedures to determine system adequacy and recommend improvements.

Experience providing accounting advice, technical guidance, and advisory services to financial managers, program managers, and other accountants on accounting systems and operations problems.

Experience developing accounting policies, procedures, directives, procedural manuals, data-collection systems, or special studies to support financial management decision-making and improve accounting operations.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Accounting Operations - Knowledge of general ledger accounting and the control/subsidiary account relationships and reconciliation techniques, including accounts receivable, accounts payable, and disbursing officer's accountability.

Financial Systems - Knowledge of the standards, architecture, and specifications of automated financial systems, including source documents, system flows, system interfaces, and related internal controls.

Financial Analysis - Knowledge of the principles, methods, and techniques of financial analysis, forecasting, and modeling to interpret quantitative and qualitative data; includes data modeling, earned value management, and evaluating key financial indicators, trends, and historical data.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

For additional information about applying to Federal positions, please click on the following link: https://www.opm.gov/frequently-asked-questions/employment-faq/federal-hiring/how-do-i-apply-for-federal-jobs/ All applicants must meet all qualification requirements by the closing date of this announcement.

As an Accountant, you will perform the following duties: Carry out complex accounting assignments and functions using a broad knowledge of Federal accounting regulations, procedures, policies, and precedents. Identify and discuss discrepancies or compliance risks with management and resolve appropriately.

Provide accounting experience by preparing recommendations for financial and accounting processes and solutions.

Ensure that standards and policies of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), Department of Commerce (DOC), Office of Management and Budget, Government Accountability Office, Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board, and Generally Accepted Accounting Principles are met by applying a broad knowledge of Automated Financial Systems.

Develop financial reports and analysis, including but not limited to: Fund Balance with Treasury reports, property and accumulated depreciation roll-forwards. Develop Government Treasury Account Symbol reports, and the Chief Financial Officers Act (CFO) financial statements, including footnotes.

Document financial impacts of complex transactions in order to advise stakeholders on impacts, risks, and recommendations on enhanced controls. Reconcile cash, labor, property, and other general ledger accounts, and correct all differences between the subsidiary ledger balances and the control account balances in the general ledger.

Identify process improvements to operational effectiveness and efficiency, as well as to minimize risk. Analyze accounting systems and functionality in order to modify and adapt accounting practices and procedures to solve a variety of accounting problems.

May require independent analysis, review, and reconciliation of financial data to ensure accuracy, reliability, and compliance with regulations.

Formulate a variety of financial reports in order to provide management information on the analysis of financial data, summary of issues and risk, and recommendations of alternatives to resolve difficult problems.
Qualification requirements in the vacancy announcements are based on the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards Handbook, which contains federal qualification standards.

This handbook is available on the Office of Personnel Management's website located at: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/ BASIC REQUIREMENTS: This position requires applicants to meet a Basic Education Requirement in addition to at least one full year (52 weeks) of specialized experience OR substitution of education for experience OR combination (if applicable) in order to be found minimally qualified.

Transcripts must be submitted with your application package. You MUST meet one of the following basic education requirements: To qualify for the 0510 series: EDUCATION: A.

Degree: Accounting; or a degree in a related field such as business administration, finance, or public administration that included or was supplemented by 24 semester hours in accounting. The 24 hours may include up to 6 hours of credit in business law. (The term "accounting" means "accounting and/or auditing" in this standard.

Similarly, "accountant" should be interpreted, generally, as "accountant and/or auditor.") OR B. Combination of education and experience: at least 4 years of experience in accounting, or an equivalent combination of accounting experience, college level education, and training that provided professional accounting knowledge.

The applicant's background must also include one of the following: Twenty-four semester hours in accounting or auditing courses of appropriate type and quality.

This can include up to 6 hours of business law; A certificate as Certified Public Accountant or a Certified Internal Auditor, obtained through written examination; or Completion of the requirements for a degree that included substantial course work in accounting or auditing, e.g., 15 semester hours, but that does not fully satisfy the 24-semester-hour requirement of paragraph A, provided that (a) the applicant has successfully worked at the full-performance level in accounting, auditing, or a related field, e.g., valuation engineering or financial institution examining; (b) a panel of at least two higher level professional accountants or auditors has determined that the applicant has demonstrated a good knowledge of accounting and of related and underlying fields that equals in breadth, depth, currency, and level of advancement that which is normally associated with successful completion of the 4-year course of study described in paragraph A; and (c) except for literal nonconformance to the requirement of 24 semester hours in accounting, the applicant's education, training, and experience fully meet the specified requirements. -AND- SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must possess one year of specialized experience equivalent in difficulty and responsibility to the next lower grade level in the Federal Service.

Specialized experience is experience that has equipped the applicant with the particular competencies/knowledge, skills and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position. This experience need not have been in the federal government.

Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations e.g., professional; philanthropic, religious; spiritual; community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies; knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

To qualify at the ZA-3 or GS-11 level: SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: In addition to meeting the Basic Requirements above, applicants must also possess one full year (52 weeks) of specialized experience equivalent to the ZA-2 or GS-09 in the Federal service.

Specialized experience MUST include all of the following: Using regulations to formulate financial and accounting reports; Developing and reconciling financial reports; and Reviewing, analyzing, and validating financial data.

OR SUBSTITUTION OF EDUCATION: 3 years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. degree or Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree. OR COMBINATION OF EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE: A combination of successfully completed graduate-level education and specialized experience may be used to meet the total experience requirements.

Note: Only graduate-level education in excess of the amount required for the next lower level may be combined with experience.

About Pleo
Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’.
The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years.
Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high.

With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together.

We're looking for a Senior Accountant / Financial Reporting specialist to join our Finance Team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help strengthen core accounting execution, audit management, and monthly consolidated results analysis while being part of a high-growth environment as we scale our financial infrastructure. If you're excited about leveraging AI and automation to redefine modern accounting with a strong focus on IFRS excellence and financial rigor, then this is the opportunity for you!
Who you’ll be working with and reporting to
You’ll report to our Accounting Associate Director and work closely with teams across the Finance organisation. You will be part of a team dedicated to technical rigor and operational efficiency, partnering with cross-functional departments to elevate our accounting processes to the next level.
What you’ll be doing

s.h: As a Senior Accountant, you will
s.t:
Prepare and post journal entries, perform balance sheet reconciliations, and drive high standards for period close improving quality and speed.
Own the preparation of audit schedules, coordinate responses to requests, and drive the closure of audit questions to ensure a predictable, well-documented process.
Deep dive into monthly results, flagging risks, unusual transactions, and key movements while providing decision-ready insights for finance leadership.
Identify accounting risks, implement practical mitigations, and strengthen internal controls to ensure our processes are scalable and accurate.
Actively leverage AI tools to improve efficiency and consistency, identifying opportunities to standardise and simplify recurring accounting work.

s.h: You’ll thrive in this role if you have
s.t:
6+ years of experience with a strong ability to apply IFRS in real-world scenarios.
Comfort working with consolidated results, analysing variances, and exercising complex accounting estimates and judgments.
Proven experience managing audits end-to-end or acting as the primary finance contact for external auditors.
A track record (or clear potential) of using AI and automation to improve accounting outcomes and efficiency.
The ability to operate effectively in a fast-changing environment with an "ownership mindset" and excellent judgment.
Strong ability to translate complex accounting issues into scalable process improvements and clear insights for stakeholders.
Why is this role a good fit for you

s.h: This role is a good fit for you if
s.t:
You want genuine agency at group level rather than executing instructions handed down by a central team
You'd rather design a process than inherit one, and you want to see your own work implemented
You like variety. This is a different topic most days, not a fixed monthly cycle

s.h: This role is not a good fit for you if
s.t:
You want a settled, mature environment where the process is set and the day looks the same. That's the clearest reason this role doesn't work out for people
You need stable priorities. It's volatile here. Several topics run at once, progress depends on other people, and priorities can change overnight
You want to stay inside accounting. A large part of the job is working with teams outside Finance and with external advisors in each country
How you’ll develop in this role

s.h: In your first 6 - 12 months at Pleo, you’ll
s.t:
Lead the Audit Readiness initiative to drive impact in our year-end execution and documentation standards.
Collaborate with the Finance team to embed AI-forward ways of working, automating manual workflows to increase team capacity.
Grow your skills in process improvements and financial analysis, taking on new challenges as the company continues to scale across our legal entity markets.
We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger leadership projects, mastering the intersection of AI and Finance, or deepening your expertise in complex consolidated reporting.

This role is hybrid (on average, 3 days a week in the office) and can be located in either our Lisbon or Madrid office.

We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows:
Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background.
Hiring manager interview: A conversation with our Accounting Associate Director covering your technical accounting and IFRS experience.
Team panel and Pleo challenge: You'll meet the hiring manager, his manager and a peer from the team. The challenge is presented live in the session, so there's nothing to prepare or send in advance. We're looking at how you handle complexity, new areas and stakeholders.
Final interview: A closing conversation, used where it's helpful for both sides.
Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success!
Last time we hired this role, we received a lot of applications but can only interview a finite number of people. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include:
CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light.

What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on.

A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background!

To qualify for the position of Accountant, at GS-0510-11, you must meet the qualification requirements listed below. Basic Entry Requirements: A. Degree: accounting; or a degree in a related field such as business administration, finance, or public administration that included or was supplemented by 24 semester hours in accounting.

The 24 hours may include up to 6 hours of credit in business law. (The term "accounting" means "accounting and/or auditing" in this standard. Similarly, "accountant" should be interpreted, generally, as "accountant and/or auditor.") -OR- B.

Combination of education and experience: at least 4 years of experience in accounting, or an equivalent combination of accounting experience, college-level education, and training that provided professional accounting knowledge.

The applicant's background must also include one of the following: Twenty-four semester hours in accounting or auditing courses of appropriate type and quality.

This can include up to 6 hours of business law; A certificate as Certified Public Accountant or a Certified Internal Auditor, obtained through written examination; or Completion of the requirements for a degree that included substantial course work in accounting or auditing, e.g., 15 semester hours, but that does not fully satisfy the 24-semester-hour requirement of paragraph A, provided that (a) the applicant has successfully worked at the full-performance level in accounting, auditing, or a related field, e.g., valuation engineering or financial institution examining; (b) a panel of at least two higher level professional accountants or auditors has determined that the applicant has demonstrated a good knowledge of accounting and of related and underlying fields that equals in breadth, depth, currency, and level of advancement that which is normally associated with successful completion of the 4-year course of study described in paragraph A; and (c) except for literal nonconformance to the requirement of 24 semester hours in accounting, the applicant's education, training, and experience fully meet the specified requirements.

Specialized Experience: Applicants must have one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-09 level.

Specialized experience is experience which is in or related to the line of work of the position to be filled and which has equipped the applicant with the specific knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.

Examples of specialized experience include: Performing analysis, validation, and reconciliation of fund accounts across multiple financial management systems; Processing and recording complex accounting transactions including obligations, disbursements, cost accruals, accounts payable/receivable, and resolving out-of-balance conditions in financial reports; Administering fund control activities including certifying fund availability, analyzing appropriated fund accounts, and tracking commitments, obligations, and expenditures; Evaluating and troubleshooting financial management information systems to identify and resolve technical accounting issues affecting data integrity and system performance; Reconciling financial data from multiple internal and external systems to ensure accuracy and compliance with federal accounting standards and reporting requirements; Preparing financial reports, trial balance reconciliations, and financial transactions supporting annual audited financial statements in compliance with governing requirements.

GS-11: Substitution of Education for Experience: A Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or three (3) full years of progressively higher-level graduate education leading to such a degree, or LL.M. if related.
